correctness.rationale: Both bipartition sides contain vertices adjacent to the entire opposite side; hence each within-side color class has odd size. If a class contains marked a_i and another A-vertex, then it has size at least three odd, while b_i sees size minus one, a positive even count, contradiction. The symmetric argument makes all marked B-endpoints singleton. Properness permits cross-side sharing only on one deleted matched pair; these conditions are also sufficient because the only missing neighbor in a matched vertex neighborhood is its paired singleton. The count is a unique decomposition into odd set partitions, chosen shared pairs, and distinct palette color names. Minimization and minimum-coloring counts follow from smallest odd-block partition counts. The even-crown edge insertion comparison is a direct two-color construction and the new formula. The actual standalone checker exhaustively checked 87,448 unlabeled partitions in 16 parameter triples and 13,795 explicit constructions, plus palette brute force.

originality.rationale: The closest actual same-invariant source is Caro et al., arXiv:2410.02336v1, Theorem 4.4. It establishes the chromatic number of K_p times K_q, including the fully deleted-matching crown K_2 times K_n. Our positive-unmatched-vertex regime t<min(m,n) is irregular and not a complete direct product, and the source does not state its chromatic number, color-class classification, all-palette polynomial, or edge-insertion jump. Targeted literature and scientific-record searches, plus own current and previous ledgers, found no equivalent or dominating statement. This is a bounded novelty assessment, not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unpublished or non-indexed exact strong odd coloring enumeration of partial matching-deleted bicliques could exist.
The two endpoint cases t=0 and t=min(m,n) have different class structures and are not claimed to satisfy this polynomial.
The repeated-color lemma in the 2024 direct-product proof is related, but that paper neither covers the irregular graph family nor its all-colorings profile.

value.rationale: The family naturally interpolates between a complete biclique and a crown graph via deleting only a nonempty proper subset of matching edges. The result supplies the full strong odd coloring polynomial in terms of odd-block set partitions, not merely a numerical chromatic bound. The positive unmatched vertices force a structural regime qualitatively absent from fully deleted-matching direct products. For every even n the insertion of one missing crown matching edge raises chi_so from 2 to n+1, demonstrating unbounded one-edge instability; this sharp motivated boundary is the substantive consequence of the general classification.
